dossiers.title: Rung 1 — Calibration: unbounded primes with a planted inequality
dossiers.statement: For every natural number n, there exists a natural prime p such that n ≤ p.
dossiers.falsifier: A natural number n for which every natural prime p is strictly less than n.
dossiers.motivation: A short, formally stated theorem lets the first ledger exercise distinguish a correct claim from a nearly identical but false one without asking reviewers to infer the target statement.
dossiers.scope: Natural numbers and Lean's Nat.Prime predicate; the exercise is only theorem-statement and review calibration.
dossiers.out_of_scope: A new proof of Euclid's theorem, prime-distribution claims, hosted proof execution, or a public correctness badge.
success_criteria: An independent reviewer identifies the reversed inequality in the planted candidate and records a refuted verdict against the candidate version.
A correctly stated claim retains its exact falsifier and an anchored citation.
The author cannot self-review or set a disposition.

sources.locator: Theorem Nat.exists_infinite_primes; declaration quantified over n : Nat.
sources.license_or_rights: Apache-2.0 for Mathlib source; this dossier stores no source body.

expected_validator_behaviors.expected: A review from the author is refused as REVIEWER_IS_AUTHOR.
Author-supplied disposition or proved-like fields are schema-invalid and cannot set the outcome.
A claim without the stated falsifier is refused before promotion.

safety_privacy: No personal data, credentials, or private workshop material.
No source body or hidden reasoning is uploaded.
dossiers.no_claim_boundary: The oracle is a test answer, not independent validation of an actual ledger claim. Only an independent staging review can establish that the calibration flow behaves as specified.

external_review_required.expertise: number theory or formal mathematics reviewer
external_review_required.independence: not the dossier author and not a reviewer of their own candidate
external_review_required.evidence: check exact quantifier and inequality against the cited Mathlib declaration and the hidden oracle

dossiers.title: Rung 2 — Reproduction: first positive zero of J₀
dossiers.statement: Using mpmath 1.3.0 with precision fixed at 80 decimal digits, compute the first positive zero j₀,₁ of the Bessel function J₀ and report a decimal value within 1e-30 absolute error of the oracle target.
dossiers.falsifier: A clean-room rerun using the pinned source artifact and stated precision whose absolute error from the oracle target exceeds 1e-30, or whose input/output digest does not match the claimed run.
dossiers.motivation: This is a small numerical reproduction with a named standard reference, a pinned open-source tool artifact, an exact numerical target, and an honest failure path.
dossiers.scope: Only j₀,₁, a CPU-only local mpmath run, and a decimal comparison at the stated tolerance.
dossiers.out_of_scope: A claim about all Bessel-zero algorithms, numerical-library performance, GPU use, or scientific discovery.
success_criteria: The reproduction evidence records the pinned mpmath source digest, precision, command, and result digest.
A second sponsor reruns the target without receiving the oracle decimal in its working pack.
A missing detection tolerance is not treated as confirmatory computation.

dossiers.title: Rung 3 — Counterexample: bounded cubic-graph Hamiltonicity
dossiers.statement: Every finite connected simple 3-regular graph with at most 10 vertices has a Hamiltonian cycle.
dossiers.falsifier: A canonical edge list for a connected simple 3-regular graph on at most 10 vertices together with an exhaustive Hamiltonian-cycle check that returns no cycle.
dossiers.motivation: A finite false conjecture exercises explicit detection floors, counterexample evidence, killed hypotheses, and preservation of a negative result without claiming an unbounded graph-theory theorem.
dossiers.scope: Simple undirected labeled graphs with at most 10 vertices; exhaustive candidate generation and cycle checking are both required.
dossiers.out_of_scope: Any claim about cubic graphs above the stated floor, a general Hamiltonicity theorem, or an inference from a sampled graph set.
success_criteria: The search manifest states the candidate space and the ≤10 detection floor before execution.
The Petersen-graph oracle is discovered or independently reconstructed and its no-cycle result is checked.
A missing floor is visibly downgraded rather than presented as exhaustive computation.

dossiers.title: Rung 4 — Formalization: Euclid's theorem in Mathlib
dossiers.statement: For every n : Nat, there exists p : Nat such that n ≤ p and Nat.Prime p.
dossiers.falsifier: A specific natural number n for which no natural prime p satisfies n ≤ p, or an independently compiled artifact whose theorem statement is not definitionally equivalent to the stated target.
dossiers.motivation: A known Mathlib theorem isolates statement equivalence, toolchain pinning, formalization friction, and independent compilation from the much harder task of formalizing a novel result.
dossiers.scope: Lean 4.33.0 and Mathlib commit db584cd6d46c92f209a44c0f1c829460d327499d; exact theorem statement only.
dossiers.out_of_scope: Hosted Lean execution, automatic certified classification, a claim that a source-library theorem validates a new ledger claim, or a general proof-assistant comparison.
success_criteria: The claimed theorem statement is checked byte-for-byte and semantically against the pinned declaration.
A deliberately weaker artifact is rejected by statement-equivalence review even if it compiles.
A friction report distinguishes missing-hypothesis, definition-mismatch, and tactic-only outcomes.

dossiers.title: Rung 5 — Literature: verification modes in four-colour theorem sources
dossiers.statement: Produce an anchored, non-exhaustive map of the verification modes reported by Appel–Haken (1977) Parts I and II, Robertson–Sanders–Seymour–Thomas (1997), and Gonthier (2008), distinguishing computer-assisted and formally checked work without ranking their authors or asserting novelty; separately catalog the cited 1977 supplement DOI metadata without inferring its primary text or page characterization pending publisher-side confirmation.
dossiers.falsifier: An included source does not support its assigned verification-mode description at the cited locator, a source is misidentified, a metadata-only source is presented as verified primary text or assigned a verification mode, or a search record reveals that the stated scope omitted a directly relevant primary source without disclosure.
dossiers.motivation: The bounded corpus makes citation anchors, rights handling, literature claims, novelty review, and synthesis anchoring testable without asking the ledger to settle the four-colour theorem.
dossiers.scope: Only Appel–Haken (1977) Parts I and II, Robertson–Sanders–Seymour–Thomas (1997), and Gonthier (2008), with their bibliographic and verification-mode descriptions, plus one 1977 supplement DOI metadata record whose primary text, page range, and characterization remain unverified pending publisher-side confirmation; citations are links plus short locators, never copied papers.
dossiers.out_of_scope: A new proof, a historical ranking, a claim that the corpus is exhaustive, or a novelty conclusion about any mathematical result.
success_criteria: Each verification-mode claim names a primary source, exact locator, retrieval date, and rights status; metadata-only entries are explicitly barred from primary-text or mode claims.
The review records the search terms and dates, nearest known work, and which claims were actually checked.
A synthesis cannot publish a verification-mode assertion that lacks an anchored ledger citation.
